items.title: Earl King Interview, 1980-04-10
items.q: That was recorded in, uh, Matt, it's two heels, this Mack Murr, and Jackson.

ctx.x: I'm talking about, at that time in 55, 56, when this phenomenon was coming out, the media was focusing on a thing called rock and roll. What's, what was it they were, they were, they were talking about?

The only difference, the only difference, what they were talking about, anything with a, a temper song was considered rock. If you played a slow song, a moderate song, that wasn't rock. If you play the same changes, you can sing the same melody. That's not rock. I mean, you, you, you, it's got to be drawing, got to be penetrating. Well, that's the studio. Like recording. Yeah, we'll use that as a good example. That was recorded in, uh, Matt, it's two heels, this Mack Murr, and Jackson. And like, you got a…

Yeah. Oftentimes, you have to record fairly quickly. Today, we're dealing with... Time conscious. Today, we deal with multi-track recording, where groups take often days and months to record. In those days, you went into the studio, and if you didn't do four songs in three hours in one session, uh... That's it. You didn't get the job done.
